The **simulation core** for running and composing simulation modules, developed for
the ARPA-H CIRCLE program **INFLECT** and built on
[Process-Bigraph](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/process-bigraph). The idea
is vivarium as a simulation core: wrap any simulator as a module behind a
**common typed API**, run modules together in simulations and workflows through that
same API, and **switch between engines** — a C++ physiology engine, an exact
SBML/Antimony model, a learned surrogate — by swapping one box, because they share
the same typed port contract.

The demonstration takes one real model, the BioGears sepsis core, and puts it through
a full capabilities screening: **compose** engines behind one interface, run
**ensembles**, **orchestrate** workflows that hand a model between engines, and
**screen performance** across them — each as a runnable artifact, not a claim.

The investigation demonstrates four capabilities on that one model — **composition**
(the same spec under three engines, swapped by one node), **ensembles** (a severity ×
engine batch in one sweep), **orchestration** (a workflow that hands an Antimony/SBML
file between engines), and **performance** (one run spans seconds to hours across
engines) — each as a runnable artifact, not a claim. A fidelity backbone keeps it
honest: the engines agree on the inflammation core to within ~0.1% and diverge in the
hemodynamic layer, where the SBML extraction reaches septic shock by a different
mechanism and on a shifted timeline.

## The unified simulation-core API

Register simulation modules, engine adapters, and API-calling steps into one
registry, then drive them from one API — as a Python import or the `viva-sim` CLI:

```python
from viva_simulation_core import catalog, call, connect, run, serve
```

Six ways to run your task, each a runnable example:

| Way | What it is | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **call** | run one engine/module | `demo_call` |
| **connect + run** | compose engines, hand a model between them | `demo_connect_run` |
| **sweep** | ensemble the same spec across a grid | `demo_sweep` |
| **serve** | a model as a stepping API | [`examples/serve_demo.py`](examples/serve_demo.py) |
| **api-call** | a step that calls a served/remote model | `serve_demo.serve_and_call` |
| **Nextflow** | vivarium inside a workflow engine | [`examples/nextflow/`](examples/nextflow/) |

See it all at once:

    uv run python -m examples.workflow_tour

Reference: [`docs/simulation-core.md`](docs/simulation-core.md).

## Getting started

You need [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (and a C/C++ toolchain only for the
optional native BioGears engine, below).

    git clone https://github.com/INFLECT-Praenora/inflect-sim-core
    cd inflect-sim-core
    uv sync                       # framework + workbench + CLI (NO engines)
    uv sync --extra all           # ...plus every simulation engine

A bare install gives you the SBML/Antimony sepsis model definition, the
digital-twin API, the workbench, the visualizations, and all committed comparison
data. **Running** a simulation needs at least one engine — pick them below.

### Simulation engines — install only what you need

The engines are **optional extras**: a bare install pulls in none of them, so you
install just the ones you want. Each is a process-bigraph-compatible wrapper
around a real solver, interchangeable behind the same API.

| Extra | Engine | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `tellurium` | Tellurium / roadrunner | exact SBML (CVODE) |
| `copasi` | COPASI (`basico`) | exact SBML |
| `biogears` | BioGears 8.2.0 | C++ whole-body physiology (native build — see below) |
| `surrogate` | viva-torch | learned PyTorch surrogate |
| `rust` | viva-core | Rust execution backend |
| `sbml` | tellurium + copasi | **bundle:** all exact-SBML engines |
| `all` | everything above | **bundle** |

```bash
# uv (uses the pinned revs in uv.lock)
uv sync --extra tellurium                   # one engine
uv sync --extra tellurium --extra copasi    # several
uv sync --extra sbml                        # all exact-SBML engines
uv sync --extra all                         # everything

# plain pip — engines resolve via direct git refs, no uv required
pip install "simulation-core[tellurium] @ git+https://github.com/INFLECT-Praenora/inflect-sim-core@main"
pip install "simulation-core[all] @ git+https://github.com/INFLECT-Praenora/inflect-sim-core@main"
```

Importing the package and rendering studies/reports works with **zero** engines
installed. Ask to *run* an engine you don't have and you get an actionable error,
never a bare `ImportError`:

```
EngineNotInstalled: the 'copasi' simulation engine is not installed. Install it with:
    pip install 'simulation-core[copasi]'
```

`viva_simulation_core.engines.available_engines()` lists what's installed;
`known_engines()` lists every engine the package can wrap.

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Fast test suite | `uv run pytest` (framework-level tests need no engine) |
| Slow / engine tests | `uv run pytest -m slow` with the relevant `--extra` (real-engine tests skip cleanly when an engine is absent) |
| Workbench (browser UI) | `bash scripts/serve.sh` |
| Unified API tour | `uv run python -m examples.workflow_tour` |
| CLI | `uv run viva-sim list` (then `call` / `workflow` / `serve` / `run`) |
| Neural surrogate (torch) | `uv sync --extra surrogate` |

### The API

One registry, four verbs, many ways to run — as a Python import or the `viva-sim`
CLI, both thin over `viva_simulation_core/api/workflow.py` + `serving.py`:

```python
from viva_simulation_core import catalog, call, connect, run, serve
```

`python -m examples.workflow_tour` runs every way end to end and prints each
result — the fastest way to see what the API does. Full reference:
[`docs/simulation-core.md`](docs/simulation-core.md).

Code lives in `viva_simulation_core/`; `build_core()` in `core.py` registers the
processes and composites.

## Reproducible dependencies — read before you upgrade

The ecosystem git dependencies are pinned to **explicit commits**, not
`branch = "main"`: the base dep (`vivarium-workbench`) and the optional engine
extras (`viva-tellurium`, `viva-copasi`, `viva-biogears`, `viva-torch`,
`viva-core`) use `@<sha>` direct git references in `pyproject.toml` (so plain
`pip install "...[engine]"` resolves them), and the transitive-only pins live in
`[tool.uv.sources]`. This is deliberate: a bare `branch = "main"` drifts — the
lockfile pins one commit while `main` moves on, so a later `uv lock --upgrade`
silently mixes incompatible versions. That is exactly what once broke the real
engine (a stale `viva-biogears` against a newer `pybiogears`, producing silent
all-NaN physiology). A `?branch=main#<sha>` form in `uv.lock` also crashes the
publish runner (AmbiguousAuthority); the lock is kept to `?rev=` form.

**So:** `uv sync` always reproduces the known-good set. To upgrade a dependency,
bump its `rev` in `pyproject.toml` **and** `pybiogears` together where they are
coupled, then `uv lock` and run the engine smoke test below.

## The real BioGears engine (optional)

The SBML side and all committed comparison data reproduce **without** BioGears.
Only the real-engine arm of the `biogears-sbml-sepsis` investigation needs the
native BioGears 8.2.0 C++ engine plus its Python bindings (`pybiogears`). Build
them together — do **not** mix a hand-built `pybiogears` with a different
`viva-biogears` than the one pinned above, or the engine silently returns NaN.

    # 1. Clone the pinned pybiogears (vivarium-collective fork):
    git clone https://github.com/vivarium-collective/pybiogears ~/code/pybiogears

    # 2. Build BioGears 8.2.0 + pybiogears together (this applies the macOS
    #    load-path repair that a plain `pip install` skips):
    ~/code/pybiogears/scripts/install_biogears.sh --with-pybiogears
    #    (installs to ~/biogears-8.2.0-install; re-running is incremental)

    # 3. If the --with-pybiogears step cannot find pip (uv venvs ship none),
    #    install the binding into THIS project's env instead:
    CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=~/biogears-8.2.0-install uv pip install -e ~/code/pybiogears

    # 4. Point the engine at its runtime data (needed for every engine run):
    export BIOGEARS_RUNTIME=~/biogears-8.2.0-install/share/biogears/runtime

**Smoke test** (must print a real `SBP=`, not `nan`):

    cd workspace/investigations/biogears-sbml-sepsis
    uv run python run_arms.py --engine engine --severity 3 --horizon-hours 0.2

If you see `SBP=nan`: the native engine and `pybiogears` are out of step with the
pinned `viva-biogears`. Rebuild `pybiogears` from the fork's current `main` and
re-run step 3 — `pybiogears` must match the `viva-biogears` commit pinned in
`pyproject.toml`.
